[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 5, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 5 at 4489 E Sahara Ave, Las Vegas, NV. Sourced from DataCenterMap, adjacent to the Switch Las Vegas 4 address on the same street. The operator publishes no power capacity figure for this building. Nevada holds 26 mapped data center facilities, of which only two have published power specifications, totaling 10.37 MW. This campus ranks third in Nevada by published megawatts, though that ranking reflects the scarcity of operator disclosure rather than comprehensive state capacity.
